```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(SurvFitSummary)
read_result <- function(...) {
  utils::read.csv(system.file(..., package = "SurvFitSummary",
                              mustWork = TRUE),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
f1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
f3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
runs <- read_result("validation", "results", "validation_summary.csv")
normal <- runs[runs$run == "normal", ]
mutation <- runs[runs$run == "mutation", ]
```

The results of SurvFitSummary are checked in three ways:

1. The unit tests (`tests/testthat`) compare every fitted model, table and
   output file with reference values computed independently, without any
   survival analysis library, by the Python scripts in
   `system.file("validation", "python", package = "SurvFitSummary")`.
2. The validation scripts (`inst/validation`) compare the package with
   closed forms, with other R packages that implement the same models
   independently, and with the Python reference, and estimate the coverage
   of the confidence intervals by simulation.
3. The reproduction scripts (`inst/reproduce`) reproduce published
   results: those of Jackson (2016) and of Royston and Parmar (2002) for the
   breast cancer data `flexsurv::bc`.

The validation and reproduction scripts write the verdict of every
comparison to the CSV files that are installed with the package and read by
this vignette. The latest run gave `r sum(normal$PASS)` PASS,
`r sum(normal$EXPLAINED)` EXPLAINED, `r sum(normal$FAIL)` FAIL and
`r sum(normal$INFO)` INFO verdicts.

## Verdicts

Each comparison is PASS if the difference from the reference is within its
tolerance, EXPLAINED if it is not but the difference is registered with its
reason and an upper bound in `explained.csv`, FAIL otherwise, and INFO for a
value reported without a reference. The tolerances of the published values
are half a unit of their last printed digit.

```{r verdicts}
knitr::kable(normal[, c("script", "PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL", "INFO")],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

## Independent routes

| Script | Comparison |
|---|---|
| `validate_survreg.R` | Exponential, Weibull, lognormal and log-logistic models against `survival::survreg()` |
| `validate_closed_forms.R` | Exponential maximum likelihood estimates in closed form; survival, hazard, median, mean and restricted mean of six distributions against their formulas |
| `validate_splines_rstpm2.R` | Spline models on the three scales against `rstpm2::stpm2()` with the same knots |
| `validate_python_reference.R` | The 12 distributions and the spline models against the independent Python implementation |

The largest difference of the comparisons that pass, as a fraction of their
tolerance, shows how much margin each comparison has.

```{r margins}
scripts <- c("validate_survreg", "validate_closed_forms",
             "validate_splines_rstpm2", "validate_python_reference")
margins <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scripts, function(s) {
  v <- read_result("validation", "results", paste0(s, ".csv"))
  p <- v[which(v$verdict == "PASS" & v$tolerance > 0), ]
  data.frame(script = s, comparisons = nrow(v),
             largest_fraction_of_tolerance = max(p$difference / p$tolerance))
}))
knitr::kable(margins, digits = 3)
```

## Published results

```{r published}
repro <- rbind(
  read_result("reproduce", "results", "reproduce_Jackson2016.csv"),
  read_result("reproduce", "results", "reproduce_RoystonParmar2002.csv")
)
compared <- repro[repro$verdict != "INFO", ]
explained <- read_result("validation", "explained.csv")
```

Of the `r nrow(compared)` published values,
`r sum(compared$verdict == "PASS")` are reproduced to their printed digits
and `r sum(compared$verdict == "EXPLAINED")` differ for the reasons
registered in `explained.csv`: the published fits of the spline models of
Jackson (2016) differ from the maximum likelihood estimates, on which the
package and `rstpm2` agree, in the third decimal of the effects and the sixth
decimal of the survival probabilities (the article computes the 5-year
survival of the odds-scale model on the hazard scale, which the reference
value takes into account), and one estimate of Royston and Parmar (2002)
lies just beyond the rounding boundary of its printed value.

```{r explained}
ex <- compared[compared$verdict == "EXPLAINED",
               c("script", "item", "reference", "value", "difference",
                 "max_difference")]
knitr::kable(ex, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(explained[, c("item", "reason")], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Mutation run

Every script is run a second time with the values of the package shifted by
0.01 * max(1, |value|) before the comparison. Every comparison must then
FAIL; a comparison that still passed would not detect an error of that size.
For this, every tolerance is at most half the shift, which the scripts check
before they compare. In the latest mutation run there were
`r sum(mutation$PASS)` PASS and `r sum(mutation$EXPLAINED)` EXPLAINED
verdicts among the `r sum(mutation$PASS + mutation$EXPLAINED + mutation$FAIL)`
comparisons.

```{r mutation}
knitr::kable(mutation[, c("script", "PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL", "INFO")],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

## Coverage of the confidence intervals

`validate_coverage.R` simulates 500 samples of 300 patients from Weibull,
lognormal and log-logistic distributions, fits each with its own
distribution (and the Weibull samples also with the spline model on the
hazard scale with 1 knot), and records whether the 95% confidence intervals
of the parameters and of the survival at 6, 12 and 24 months contain the
true values.

```{r coverage}
cov <- read_result("validation", "results", "validate_coverage.csv")
coverage <- cov[grepl("coverage of the 95% CI", cov$item), ]
mc_se <- cov$value[grepl("Monte Carlo", cov$item)]
knitr::kable(data.frame(interval = coverage$item,
                        coverage = coverage$value),
             digits = 3)
```

The coverage ranges from `r f3(min(coverage$value))` to
`r f3(max(coverage$value))`, within
`r f1(max(abs(coverage$value - 0.95)) / mc_se)` Monte Carlo standard errors
(`r f3(mc_se)`) of 0.95.

## Excel workbook and Word report

`validate_outputs.R` writes the workbook and the report of the example data
with all the default models, and the Python scripts `check_workbook.py` and
`check_report.py` check their numbers against the data and the reference
values, and the numbering of the tables and figures of the report.

```{r outputs, include = FALSE}
wb <- read_result("validation", "results", "outputs", "check_workbook.csv")
rp <- read_result("validation", "results", "outputs", "check_report.csv")
wb_m <- read_result("validation", "results", "outputs", "mutation",
                    "check_workbook.csv")
rp_m <- read_result("validation", "results", "outputs", "mutation",
                    "check_report.csv")
```

`r sum(wb$verdict == "PASS")` of the `r nrow(wb)` checks of the workbook and
`r sum(rp$verdict == "PASS")` of the `r nrow(rp)` checks of the report pass.
With every number of the files shifted as in the mutation run,
`r sum(wb_m$verdict == "FAIL")` of the `r nrow(wb_m)` checks of the workbook
and `r sum(rp_m$verdict == "FAIL")` of the `r nrow(rp_m)` checks of the
numbers of the report fail.

## Running the validation

The scripts are run from the root of the source package after
`devtools::load_all()`; `validate_splines_rstpm2.R` needs the package
rstpm2, which SurvFitSummary itself does not use.

```{r run, eval = FALSE}
source(file.path("inst", "validation", "run_validation.R"))
source(file.path("inst", "validation", "validate_coverage.R"))
source(file.path("inst", "validation", "validate_outputs.R"))
```

## References

Jackson C (2016). flexsurv: A platform for parametric survival modeling in
R. Journal of Statistical Software 70(8):1-33.

Royston P, Parmar MKB (2002). Flexible parametric proportional-hazards and
proportional-odds models for censored survival data, with application to
prognostic modelling and estimation of treatment effects. Statistics in
Medicine 21(15):2175-2197.
